TF-IDF stands for Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency. [Source 1]

TF-IDF jest needed w celu zapobiegania nadmiernej wagie słów, które pojawiają się w każdym tekście, takich jak 'the' lub 'and'. IDF (Inverse Document Frequency) pomaga ustalić, ile rzeczywistego znaczenia ma dany słów w całości dokumentu. [Source 1]
We calculate IDF as the logarithm of the total number of documents divided by the number of documents containing that specific term. [Source 2]

TF-IDF is better than a simple Bag of Words count because when you multiply TF by IDF, you get a score where high values mean the word is both frequent in your document and rare in the rest of the collection, which is way better than a simple count that doesn't care about word importance [Source 2].
Dijkstra's algorithm is used for finding the shortest path between nodes in a graph, where the edge weights are non-negative. [Source 3]

Edge relaxation in Dijkstra's algorithm is the process of updating the cost of each edge in the graph as the algorithm explores the nodes, with the goal of finding the shortest path from the start node to the goal node. [Source 3]

Dijkstra’s algorithm requires non-negative edge weights because if the edge weights can be negative, it would allow the algorithm to "short-cut" the path by always choosing the edge with the negative weight, even if it leads to a longer path in the long run, which would not be the shortest path. [Source 1]
Dijkstra's algorithm is similar to A*, but if you set h(n) = 0 for every node, A* behaves exactly like Dijkstra's algorithm. [Source 1]

Binary search is the go-to algorithm when you need to find something in a sorted list very quickly. Instead of checking every single element from the beginning (which is called Linear Search), we use a divide-and-conquer strategy. We look at the middle element of the array. If the middle is exactly what we are looking for, we are done. If our target is smaller, we throw away the right half of the array and repeat the process on the left half. If it's larger, we focus on the right half. [Source 1]
The time complexity of binary search is O(log n), which is incredibly fast compared to O(n) for linear search. [Source 1]

DFS can be used for topological sorting by ordering the nodes by decreasing DFS finish time in a directed acyclic graph (DAG). This is because DFS naturally explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, allowing it to assign a finish time to each node. By ordering the nodes by decreasing finish time, a valid topological order can be obtained, which is how build systems decide in which order to compile dependencies [Source 2].
